common.noResultsHint: Try removing or changing the filters to see more.

auth.identifierHelp: Use the email — or the username — your hotel gave you.
auth.setupDetailsNote: Your name and hotel come from your invitation — you can update your name later from My Profile.

profile.intro: Your personal details and sign-in settings. Changes here affect only your own account.
profile.languageHelp: Controls the dashboard language for you, and the language of emails we send you.
profile.emailHelp: The email you sign in with — it can't be changed from here.
profile.roleTip: Your role decides which pages and actions are available to you. Roles are managed from the Roles page by the hotel administrator.

staff.intro: Everyone who can sign in to this dashboard. Invite staff by email, or create accounts directly for team members without one.
staff.firstRunBody: Invite by email lets the person activate their own account and choose a password. Create directly gives you a username and a temporary password to hand over — best for on-ground staff without email.

status.pending: An invitation was sent but the account hasn't been activated yet. You can resend the invite from this row.
status.active: The account is activated and this member can sign in.
status.disabled: Access is switched off. The member's data and history are kept — you can re-enable them here at any time.

staff.lastLoginTip: When this member last signed in. "Never" means they haven't signed in yet.

form.roleHelp: Decides which pages and actions this member can use. You can change it later, or manage roles from the Roles page.

roles.intro: Roles decide what each staff member can see and do. Create a role per job — reception, housekeeping — then assign it when adding staff.
roles.firstRunBody: Each staff member holds one role, and the role's permissions decide which pages and actions they get. Editing a role applies to everyone holding it immediately.
roles.systemTip: Created automatically with the hotel. It can't be edited, deleted or assigned to staff — and it always keeps full access.
roles.nameHelp: Staff see the role name in their own language, so fill in both.
roles.descriptionHelp: Optional — one sentence to remind you what this role is for.
roles.permissionsHelp: Pick what this role can see and do. You can change it later — changes reach everyone holding the role immediately.

home.setupSubtitle: A few steps to set up your hotel — each one takes a minute. Steps check off automatically as you complete them.
home.stepAddStaffHint: Invite your team by email, or create accounts with a username for staff without one.
home.stepCreateRole: Create a role for your team
home.stepCreateRoleHint: Roles decide what each staff member can see and do.
home.stepAddRoomsHint: Rooms are what guests scan to reach your services — add them one at a time, in a number range, or import from Excel.
home.stepPrintQrHint: Generate a printable PDF of QR cards for your rooms — one per door.

rooms.intro: Rooms are what guests scan to reach your services. Add them one at a time, in a number range, or import from Excel — each active room gets its own QR code linking straight to your guest app.
rooms.firstRunBody: Every room needs a room type and a status. Active and out-of-service rooms count toward your plan's room limit; inactive rooms don't. Print QR codes any time from the QR page.

status.active: Guests can scan this room's QR code and reach your services. Counts toward your plan's room limit.
status.out_of_service: Temporarily unavailable to guests — use this for rooms under maintenance. Still counts toward your plan's room limit.
status.inactive: Hidden from guests and doesn't count toward your plan's room limit. Use this for rooms removed from service long-term.

rooms.renumber: Changing this room's number invalidates any cards already printed with the old number — reprint them so guests scan the right room.
rooms.bulkPreviewNote: Review every row before confirming — rows with errors are skipped, and numbers that already exist are flagged as duplicates.
rooms.importNote: Upload an Excel file matching the template. You'll see a preview with any row errors before anything is created.
rooms.emptyOnboarding: Add your rooms to activate guest services.
rooms.qrStable: Room QR codes never change or expire — reprint them anytime without affecting how guests reach your services.
rooms.qrPrintIntro: Download print-ready materials: a general poster QR for shared spaces like your lobby, and individual QR cards for each room door.
rooms.balance: An unsettled room-charge balance — orders and requests billed to the room that haven't been paid or settled yet. Cash orders are already paid and never count here.

types.intro: Room types group similar rooms — Standard, Deluxe, Suite — so you can assign one when adding rooms and keep guest-facing details consistent.
types.nameHelp: Staff and guests see the room type name in their own language, so fill in both.

stays.intro: Check guests in, hand them their stay code, and manage everything about their stay — extensions, room moves, and checkout — from here.
stays.firstRunBody: Checking a guest in creates a 6-digit stay code — their key to the guest app. Each room holds one active stay; checkout (by you, or automatic at your checkout hour) ends the guest's app access instantly.
stays.emptyOnboarding: Check in your first guest to hand them their app access code.

status.active: The guest is currently checked in and their stay code opens the guest app.
status.checked_out: The stay has ended and its code no longer works. Past stays are kept as a permanent record and can't be changed.

checkoutType.manual: The front desk ended this stay.
checkoutType.automatic: The stay ended automatically after its check-out date passed your hotel's checkout hour.

stays.nightsColumn: Nights until the check-out date, counted in your hotel's local time.
stays.codeNote: Codes are stored securely and can't be viewed after check-in — if a guest forgets theirs, generate a new one.
stays.settingsIntro: The daily hour when overdue stays end automatically.
stays.occupancyVacant: No active stay — this room is free for check-in.
stays.balance: An unsettled room-charge balance — orders and requests billed to the room that haven't been paid or settled yet. Cash orders are already paid and never count here.

status.new: Just arrived from the guest app — nobody has started on it yet.
status.in_progress: A staff member pressed Start and owns it now.
status.done: Completed — it stays in the history permanently.
status.cancelled: Cancelled by staff (with a reason) or by the guest before work started.

requests.sla: Each request carries a time target from the catalog. The chip turns amber at 80% of the target and red once it's overdue — overdue cards float to the top.
requests.noteLanguage: The note is in the guest's language — automatic translation is coming soon.
requests.customItem: A custom item your hotel added — you own its names and translations.

stats.open: Requests currently new or in progress.
stats.doneToday: Requests completed since midnight, hotel time.
stats.overdueNow: Open requests already past their time target.

stats.open: Orders not yet delivered — received, preparing or on the way.
stats.deliveredToday: Orders delivered since midnight, hotel time.
stats.revenueToday: Paid totals of orders delivered today — cash and room-charge together. Included items count as 0.

hotelInfo.intro: Everything guests usually ask the desk — WiFi, hours, services — one tile in their app, in their language.

hint.title: Start with WiFi and facility hours
hint.body: They answer 80% of what guests ask the desk. Fill Essentials first, then add facilities with opening hours — guests see a live “Open now” badge.

branding.intro: Make the guest app unmistakably yours — pick your accent color, add a cover photo, and write a welcome line. The design system keeps everything readable.

hint.title: Three knobs, zero design skills
hint.body: Changes preview instantly on the phone mock and reach your guests within a minute of saving.

announcements.intro: Speak to your guests in their app — pool closures, schedule changes, tonight's plans — targeted so the right rooms hear it.

hint.title: The audience is a filter, not a list
hint.body: A guest checking in tonight who matches your filter sees the announcement too, as long as it's active. The recipient count is labeled "currently" for exactly that reason.

announcements.dynamicAudience: The audience is a live filter, not a snapshot — a guest checking in tonight who matches it will also see this announcement while it's active.
announcements.priority: Use sparingly. Important notices pin to the top of the guest inbox and surface on their home screen — too many and guests stop noticing.
announcements.readStats: Reads over guests currently matching the audience — the denominator moves as guests check in and out.
announcements.editLocked: Live announcements can't be edited — guests may have read the original. Retract it and send a new one instead.
announcements.activeUntil: After this time the notice leaves guest inboxes automatically — expired operational notices are just noise.
announcements.infoLink: Guests see a tappable chip that opens the linked Hotel Info entry.

status.draft: Not visible to guests. Edit it, then send or schedule.
status.scheduled: Goes live automatically at the hotel-local time you chose. Editable until then.
status.live: Visible to every guest matching the audience right now.
status.retracted: Pulled back — it left all guest inboxes immediately. Read stats are preserved.
status.expired: Its active-until time passed and it left guest inboxes automatically.

events.intro: Host workshops, tastings and get-togethers — guests browse and reserve a spot right from their phones, and you track who's coming.

hint.title: Publishing locks the schedule and price
hint.body: Get the schedule and price right before you publish — once an event is published, guests may already be booked, so its date, time, price, pricing mode and location can no longer be changed. To fix any of those, cancel the event and create a new one.

status.draft: Not visible to guests yet. Finish the details, then publish.
status.published: Live on the guest Events tile — guests can browse it and book a spot.
status.completed: Its time passed — it's closed to new bookings now and kept for the record.
status.cancelled: Cancelled — booked guests were notified and their bookings were released.

attendees.intro: Live list of everyone who booked a spot, with totals that update as guests book or cancel. Read-only.

totals.booked: Sum of party sizes across active bookings. Cancelled bookings release their spot and stop counting immediately.
totals.cash: Active cash bookings' total value — collected in person, so every one of them stays expected until it's cancelled.
totals.roomCharge: Active room-charge bookings' total value. Once one posts to the guest's folio at checkout, it drops out of this figure so it isn't counted twice.

status.clean: Nothing to do here — the room was cleaned and nothing has flagged it since. New rooms start clean.
status.needs_cleaning: Waiting for a clean. Checkout flags appear automatically when a stay ends; daily flags each morning at your daily service hour for occupied rooms.
status.in_progress: An attendant pressed Start and owns this room right now. Starting an unassigned room assigns it to you.
status.dnd: The guest switched on Do-Not-Disturb in their app. Cleaning can't start until it lifts — it clears automatically at the next daily service hour, at checkout, or when the guest turns it off.

stats.toClean: Rooms currently flagged for cleaning — checkout turnovers and daily stay-over service.
stats.inProgress: Rooms an attendant is cleaning right now.
stats.doneToday: Rooms finished since midnight, hotel time — the shift's progress bar.
stats.dnd: Rooms the guest asked not to disturb today. The daily round skips them.

housekeeping.dnd: The guest asked not to be disturbed today. Do-Not-Disturb lifts automatically at the next daily service hour (or at checkout) — you can still assign the room or park a flag for later.
housekeeping.settingsIntro: Each morning at this hour, occupied rooms flag themselves for daily service and Do-Not-Disturb lifts — in your hotel's local time.

reports.housekeepingWorkload: Shown to understand today's workload distribution across the team — not a performance ranking.
reports.busiestHoursTip: Shows how guest requests are distributed across the day, in your hotel's local time — use it to staff shifts around your peak hours.
